evidence: src/refresh-token/refresh-token.service.ts: every public method of RefreshTokenService works on RefreshToken (generate, resolve, decode, getRefreshTokenByUserId, revokeRefreshTokenById, getRefreshTokenGroupedData), so the file has one concern.
src/refresh-token/refresh-token.service.ts: data access mostly uses RefreshTokenRepository (createRefreshToken, findTokenById, getPaginationInfo, transformMany).
src/refresh-token/refresh-token.service.ts: revokeRefreshTokenById calls token.save() (the entity saves itself) instead of going through the repository, a minor inconsistency.
src/refresh-token/refresh-token.service.ts: 'not found' is raised as CustomHttpException(ExceptionTitleList.NotFound) in resolveRefreshToken but as NotFoundException in revokeRefreshTokenById.

src/refresh-token/refresh-token.service.ts: the same CustomHttpException(ExceptionTitleList.InvalidRefreshToken, HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, StatusCodesList.InvalidRefreshToken) is built inline five times.

src/refresh-token/refresh-token.service.ts: getRefreshTokenByUserId builds the active-token filter {isRevoked: false, expires: MoreThanOrEqual(new Date())} inline instead of calling a repository method.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is one file, src/refresh-token/refresh-token.service.ts, and it covers one concern: the refresh-token lifecycle. Its methods issue a token (generateRefreshToken), resolve and decode it (resolveRefreshToken, decodeRefreshToken, getUserFromRefreshTokenPayload, getStoredTokenFromRefreshTokenPayload), exchange it for an access token (createAccessTokenFromRefreshToken), list a user's active tokens (getRefreshTokenByUserId), revoke one (revokeRefreshTokenById) and aggregate statistics (getRefreshTokenGroupedData). Data access mostly goes through RefreshTokenRepository (createRefreshToken, findTokenById, getPaginationInfo, transformMany, and inherited findAndCount and createQueryBuilder). Its token-format rules are kept in one place: BASE_OPTIONS and the decode logic.

There are some minor inconsistencies:
- revokeRefreshTokenById saves through the entity itself with token.save() instead of the repository.
- "Not found" is reported two ways: CustomHttpException(ExceptionTitleList.NotFound, ...) in resolveRefreshToken and NotFoundException in revokeRefreshTokenById.
- The identical InvalidRefreshToken CustomHttpException is built inline five times.
- The "active token" filter (isRevoked false, expires >= now) is built inline in the service instead of in a repository method.

These are local code-quality smells, not a split into unrelated concerns or a clear bypass of the module's abstraction. On balance the unit passes the rule.
